statement:
Solve the following system of equations in real numbers:
\[\begin{cases} \sqrt{x^2-2x+6} \cdot \log_3(6-y) = x \\ \sqrt{y^2-2y+6} \cdot \log_3(6-z) = y \\ \sqrt{z^2-2z+6} \cdot \log_3(6-x) = z \end{cases}\]

Let \(ABCD\) be a convex quadrilateral. Take an arbitrary point \(M\) on line \(AB\) and let \(N\) be the second intersection of the circumcircles of \(\triangle MAC\) and \(\triangle MBC\). Prove that:\\
a) The point \(N\) lies on a fixed circle.\\
b) The line \(MN\) passes through a fixed point.

Let \(m, n > 3\) be positive integers. Consider an \(m \times n\) grid. We place 4 marbles at a time into unit squares (one per square) forming specific L-shaped or square tetrominoes. Is it possible, after finitely many steps, to place exactly one marble in every cell?\\
a) \(m = 2004\), \(n = 2006\).\\
b) \(m = 2005\), \(n = 2006\).

Given \(f(x) = -x + \sqrt{(x+a)(x+b)}\) where \(a, b\) are distinct positive reals. Prove that for all \(s \in (0,1)\) there exists a unique positive real \(\alpha\) such that \(f(\alpha) = s\,\sqrt[s]{\dfrac{a^s+b^s}{2}}\).

Find all polynomials \(P(x)\) with real coefficients satisfying
\[P(x^2) + x(3P(x) + P(-x)) = (P(x))^2 + 2x^2\]
for all real \(x\).

Let \(S\) be a set of 2006 numbers. Call a subset \(T \subseteq S\) \emph{naughty} if for any \(u, v \in T\) (not necessarily distinct), \(u + v \notin T\). Prove that:\\
1) If \(S = \{1, 2, \ldots, 2006\}\), every naughty subset has at most 1003 elements.\\
2) If \(S\) is any set of 2006 positive integers, there exists a naughty subset with at least 669 elements.
